facts.claim: Federal rebate for installing an electric heat pump. $2 billion over eight years, aimed at up to 820,000 households.
facts.eligibility: Income cut-off, home types and which heating fuels qualify are not published yet. The federal government cites average savings of more than $1,400 a year for homes using oil, propane or electric resistance heat. One rebate per person. Heat pump must be on the Eligible Products List (over 100,000 options).
facts.notes: Also https://www.pm.gc.ca/en/news/news-releases/2026/10/08/prime-minister-carney-announces-landmark-investment-retrofit-one and https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/campaigns/one-million-home-energy-retrofits.html. Canada.ca campaign page says amounts and launch dates will be sent to people who sign up.

facts.claim: Government expects to launch early 2027 and is 'eyeing' making the rebate retroactive to fall 2026.
facts.eligibility: Retroactivity is NOT confirmed. It is reported by CBC (read in full text supplied 2026-10-09), not stated in the canada.ca release.
facts.notes: Recheck canada.ca campaign page weekly until the portal opens. Federal officials are consulting HVAC industry before launch.

facts.claim: Apply in an online portal when the existing heating system breaks or nears end of life. Approval within 24 hours, then buy and install a pre-approved heat pump, upload receipts, payment approved within five days by direct deposit. No pre- or post-installation energy audit.
facts.eligibility: Government data cited by CBC: 80 per cent of HVAC replacements happen when the system breaks.
facts.notes: Direct deposit and 'receipts after installation' from CBC reading of the government document, 2026-10-09.

facts.claim: Federal government says the rebates can be combined with existing provincial programs.
facts.eligibility: Each provincial program's own rules on stacking with federal money have not been read against this new program.

facts.claim: Free, direct-install retrofits (insulation, heat pumps) for low-to-median-income homeowners and tenants, delivered through provinces. Moving to Environment and Climate Change Canada. Apply through your province, not the federal government.
facts.eligibility: Provinces accepting applications on the NRCan page: British Columbia, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, Quebec.
facts.notes: Page last updated August 31, 2026. Different program from the National Heat Pump Rebate.

facts.program: Federal apartment and rental retrofit programs
facts.claim: CMHC mortgage insurance product supporting up to 250,000 rental units, Canada Infrastructure Bank financing for 30,000 more units, and a Deep Retrofit Accelerator of $110 million over three years starting 2027-28. About 280,000 apartment units to be retrofitted over eight years.
facts.eligibility: For building owners, not individual tenants.
